THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:5337  WP No. 103171 of 2023  ORDER Heard Sri Roshan Chabbi, Advocate appearing for Sri Shivraj S.Balloli, learned counsel for petitioners.
Learned AGA for respondents on advance notice opposes petition.
2. This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs.

It was submitted that petitioners were absolute owners of property bearing no.4-1-8-73C situated at Ward no.4, Hosapete, which originally belonged to father of petitioners who had bequeathed it in favour of mother of petitioners under a Will to enable her to enjoy same during her lifetime.

Thereafter, it was to belong to petitioner no.1.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:5337 4.
It was submitted that after death of petitioners' father, name of petitioner is entered in revenue records.
But one Smt.Shamshad Begum got her name fraudulently entered in respect of petitioner and also got executed a Will in her favour.

It was submitted said claim was based on fraudulent sale deed at Annexure-E and therefore petitioners had filed complaint before Hosapete Town Police Station, Hosapete registered in Crime no.132/2020 for offences punishable under Sections 420,
465, 467, 466, 471 and Section 120-B r/w Section 34 of I.P.C. against respondent no.4 herein.

3 5.

sentences.text: Based on same, petitioners had also submitted representation as per Annexure-H dated 15.11.2021 for cancellation of fraudulent sale deed.

In response and without proper consideration,
impugned endorsement at Annexure-A dated 13.12.2021 is issued.
Endorsement refusing to consider representation for cancellation of sale deed would be unjustified and arbitrary and therefore, sought for allowing writ petition.
Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition records.
7. From above, it is seen that petitioner claims to be aggrieved by registration of sale deeds by respondent no.3.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Satyapal Anand V/s State of Madhya Pradesh and others reported in 2016(10) SCC 767 has held that registering authority has no power for cancellation of sale deed and only remedy for aggrieved party would be to approach appropriate Civil Court for relief Section 31 of Specific Relief Act.

entities.text: Satyapal Anand V/s State of Madhya Pradesh and others reported in 2016(10) SCC 767
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such being case, writ petition challenging endorsement would not be tenable.
8. Hence, writ petition is dismissed.

However, it is clarified that rejection of petitioners'
representation and dismissal of present petition would not come in way of petitioner urging all contentions before Civil Court.
Sd/-
